items.note: S1.3 states a fixed network of pointwise linear gates on triples that exchanges the banks in three stages and restores every scratch wire, quoting the forward invocation y_S+x_S (line 730). It omits h=100, N, m, the neighbour rules and the eight-row schedule, and calls the result an exchange without the sign: the complex network gives (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a). The cancellation argument is not shown.

S1.4 gives the mechanism correctly: a common frame commutes with a pointwise gate, so only the endpoint frames fix the net operator and edges only change frame. It does not give the edge operator D_vD_u^{-1} or the identity D_out S D_in^{-1} / eps_w D_sink D_source^{-1}.

S1.5.1 states that labels are comparable along edges, that only the central returns decrease, and that the sum of absolute changes is Wm-2N+2L with L<N/2, all as in the paper. It omits L=Ich, the loss h per central edge (time 3 to 4) and the ratios 100/539 and 101/539. The S1.5 method names the route (labels from triple indicators, checking nesting) but has no sub-steps for the label table or the telescoping.

S1.5.2 states the permutation rho, the endpoint difference I_m on every role and s<Wm. It omits s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b and describes all terminal matrices as projections, although the X_a sources carry -P_{U_a}, which the endpoint identity needs. The shear H<-H+D appears in the S1 method.

S2.1 states that phase frames C_U make each edge a product of translation kernels aI+bX_v, and S2.3 gives s_c children. Missing: one kernel per orthonormal residual vector, the formula s_c=W_cm-2N+2L_c<W_cm, and the telescoping to C^{tensor m} on every role after corrections.

The plan states s<Wm (bit network) and s/W<m^tau with tau<1. It never gives tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, the deficits eta_b and eta_c, or the argument from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20, and it does not state s_c<W_cm.

S1.1 and S1.2 state the O(V) elementary operations, the controlled shift y+a mod q^b with b^{O(1)} offset preparation, and the multiplication by a unit, all faithfully. S1.2 also notes the split-and-merge mechanism (lines 575-581).

Both statements are correct, and the method follows the paper: factor A=E_1 Pi E_2, run the triangular parts as controlled shifts, one interchange per entry of Pi. Missing: the elimination proof of the factorization, the choice of prime q, and the D<-D+H, swap, D<-H-D trick that makes each H_i+=D_j cost exactly one interchange.

The plan follows the paper's route (bit network with shear frames, each edge by recursive interchanges, then the recurrence), and S1.7 states F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1) => O(e^tau) correctly. It omits the cyclic row split into W role streams, the conversion of the shear into an interchange (D<-D-H, H<-H+D, D<-H-D) and the fixed-tape depth-first schedule that bounds the node overhead by O(V).
S1 and S1.8 state the O(Vu^tau) bound for arbitrary equal widths, with the base-m decomposition and row padding sketched. 'Padding to power widths' is loose (see errors). There are no sub-steps.

S2.3 states s_c children on e/m axes, S2.1 states H_0^{tensor D}=b^D S_D C^{tensor D} S_D, and S2 names the binary basis changes. Missing: the conjugation by P_M that puts residual directions in coordinate slots, and the handling of inverse kernels.

The route matches the paper: eight conditional additions whose two 3-cycles flip u's parity and restore w, a payload-independent bad set B, and repair of B by sorting only its records. Imprecise: delta_bad=min{1,80(f-1)2^{-K}} and the general time bound are not given. Partial: the guard interval, the T_0S_0^{-1} argument and the separate treatment of j_{f-1} are missing. S2.2.3 also misdescribes the rotations (see errors).

S2.3 gives the child structure (s_c children on e/m axes, volume 1/W_c), and S2.4 says 'the row construction and the recurrence' give O(Vd^{lambda'}). The recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), its leaves and the exponent conditions are never stated.

S2 and S2.4 state H_0 on one common bit of each of D<=d chunks, cost O(Vd^{lambda'}), exact intermediates, and one truncation with error <sqrt2 2^{-p}. Missing: K=floor(d^c), the parameter conditions and the guard width Delta=o(p) that makes exact evaluation affordable.

S3.1 to S3.3 state omega_t=y^{2r/t} and F^+F^-=I/t, the bit-reversed output B_tF_t^- consumed by F^+B^{-1}, the layout L and the cost bound, all correctly. Missing: the per-procedure error <sqrt2 l 2^{-p} and the explicit exact counterparts LBF^- and F^+B^{-1}L^{-1}.
S3.4 matches the lemma: evaluation at 2^{4p}, products with the established multiplier, signed coefficient extraction, O(rp log(rp)). It is exact.

Statement correct: M_r=(f*g)/T, retained LB order, the error bound and the cost. The S3 method and motivation give the paper's key reason (a common record permutation commutes with the pointwise product). Missing: the exact scale by M and the error and disk-margin accounting.

S4.1 and S4.2 state P_sF_s=2^{2alpha^2}B_0P_tF_tA under theta>p/alpha^4, the error p^2, the cost, and the tensor form RF_s=2^gamma B_0 Q F_t A. Missing: the definitions of P_s, P_t, gamma=2d alpha^2 and the axis-exposure cost O(Tpd^2(1+l^tau)). The Gaussian construction is not derived.

S4.3 and S4.4 give QF_t u=abar.(a*(abar.u))/T (through the quote) and the cancellation identity u*v/S^2 correctly. Missing: the chirp a_j=exp(-pi i sum s_i j_i^2/t_i) and the conjugation that yields RF^+.

The sizes, the prime interval, alpha, T/2<S<T and alpha^4 theta>p are stated correctly, and the method follows the paper. Missing: the fixed rational exponents (tau, lambda, c, lambda', epsilon, delta), eta=1/(4d), the prime-existence argument, and the chain theta>eta that gives alpha^4 theta>p.

Phi, mu_i, the triangular b_i formula, the prefix-controlled shifts and the cost are all stated correctly. The method names the bijection proof but omits its reason: the image of x has order S because the mu_i are units and the s_i are coprime.
S5.4 states the twist by e^{pi i k/r} into C[y]/(y^r+1) and the correct wrap after untwisting. Missing: M_C=D_- iota^{-1} M_r(iota D_+ f, iota D_+ g)=(f*g)/T and the twist error bounds.

S5, S5.5 and S5.6 give the source transform (A, chirp transform, B_0, 2^gamma; counterpart RF_s) and the six algorithm steps. S5.6 lists the second rescaling as 2^{2b+4} instead of 2^{2b+4}S, and the input scaling by 2^{-b-2} and the conjugation for F^+ are not given.

The chain 5TL, 6TL, 8TL, E_s, E_w, 448b2^{-3b/4}<1/2, then carries, follows the paper with correct constants. Missing: the intermediate bound 448b 2^{-b+gamma} with gamma<=b/4, which is where gamma=o(b) is used, and the disk-margin bookkeeping. S5.7.3 also speaks of a 'second' pointwise product.

The margins g_1..g_7, min=2^{-181}=2kappa, setup o(V), log p<=p^kappa and the schoolbook cutoff all match the paper. The table of normalized costs (dK, pK^{tau-1}, l d^{lambda'}, ...) and the formulas for most g_i are not given, so the margins cannot be checked from the plan.
S0 says the bound refutes the n log n conjecture in this model but does not give the liminf criterion or the eventual-lower-bound formulation.

errors.says: motivation: 'each recursive call spends fewer than m units of cost per wire'
errors.paper: The saving is that the number of recursive calls per wire averages below m: s/W<m, since the sum of edge ranks s<Wm; each call acts on volume V/W.

errors.says: 'With rational projection matrices at gates and terminals' the endpoint difference is I_m
errors.paper: The X_a sources get the negated projection -P_{U_a}. This is essential to the endpoint identity and adds N source ranks, which is why s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b.

errors.says: 'Padding to power widths and enough rows'
errors.paper: Widths are not padded to powers. Binary ranges are padded to [q^e], rows are padded to a multiple of W^k, and the remaining width is decomposed in base m into power-width pieces.

errors.says: 'Each shift is a chunk interchange costing O(VL^tau)'
errors.paper: Each rotation is an O(V) controlled cyclic shift. At most sixteen chunk swaps, each O(VL^tau), move the target into place and back.
The second rescaling multiplies by 2^{2b+4}S. The two factors S undo different normalizations.

errors.says: 'After the second pointwise product and the opposite transform'
errors.paper: The algorithm has one pointwise product, z=Q_p(U~.V~_1), followed by the opposite transform.

chain: The plan reaches the main bound by the paper's route: bit network, frames, labels, matrix shear, recurrence for the interchange; complex phase frames, packed additions and a layer recurrence for the butterflies; then synthetic convolution, resampling, chirp, CRT, exact recovery and the margin table. It is thinnest at the core saving: the label budget is stated without L=Ich, the bit rank sum without its -N+2L form, and tau without its value. The butterfly side never writes out the layer recurrence F(e)<=(s/W)F(e/m)+O((eK)^tau+1), and the cost table behind the margins g_i is not reproduced.

steps.note: The network over triples, its three stages, the exchange of banks and the restoration of scratch wires are named. The plan omits h=100, the indexing by T^3 with N=binom(h,3)^3 and m=h^3, and the signed map (X_a,Y_a)->(-Y_a,X_a).

S1.4 carries the mechanism: a common invertible frame commutes with the pointwise gate, so only the endpoint frames fix the operator and each edge only changes frame. The explicit D_out S D_in^{-1} is not written.

The plan has tensor-product subspace labels from triple indicators in an m-dimensional space, nondegenerate and comparable along every edge, with only the central-wire returns decreasing. The loss of h per such edge (time 3 to 4) is missing, so this verdict is borderline.

The S1.5 method converts dimension changes into ranks of projection differences, and its motivation says nested labels cost rank only where dimension changes. It never states rank(P_V-P_U)=dim V-dim U, and it omits the N rank-one source-edge exceptions.
The plan states sum|Delta dim|=Wm-2N+2L. It does not give L=Ich or s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b, so the budget is not carried through to the rank sum.
The plan has L<N/2 and s<Wm, but not L/N=100/539 (or 101/539), nor the deficit N-2L>0 that connects them. Without the +N source term it does not explain why L<N/2 is the needed threshold.
S1.5.2 states endpoint difference I_m on every role, and the S1 method realizes the shear H<-H+D on every role. The -P_{U_a} source matrices behind the identity are not mentioned.
S1.6 and its sub-steps give A=E_1 Pi E_2 and exactly a interchanges plus O(V). S1 and S1.7 make each edge recursive interchanges, s calls in all.
S1.7 gives children of volume V/W, F_k<=(s/W)F_{k-1}+O(1), s/W<m^tau and F_k=O(e^tau). It omits the explicit tau=1-2^{-50} and its derivation from eta>20*2^{-50} and log m<20.

central.summary: The plan reconstructs the frame principle, the nested labels, the endpoint identity, the edges-as-recursive-calls step and the recurrence (C2, C3, C7, C8, C9). The quantitative core is only named: the network's parameters, rank equal to dimension change with the N source exceptions, the budget L=Ich and s_b=W_bm-N+2L_b, and the ratio 100/539 (C1, C4, C5, C6). A reader learns that s<Wm and that this gives e^tau, but not why s<Wm holds.
